details: Bitcoin extended its recovery, trading above $64,000, supported by an improvement in overall risk sentiment. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded notable net inflows of $85.9 million on Friday, marking their strongest daily intake since mid-May, which suggests a recovery in institutional demand. Optimism surrounding a potential U.S.-Iran peace agreement also contributed to the upward momentum.
title: Bitcoin Rises Above $64K as ETF Inflows Rebound Amid US-Iran Peace Hopes

details: Global financial markets are preparing for a "central bank super week," with key interest rate decisions expected from the U.S. Federal Reserve (the first under new Chair Kevin Warsh), the Bank of Japan, and the Bank of England. The Bank of Japan is widely expected to hike rates, while the Bank of England is anticipated to hold steady. The Federal Reserve is also highly likely to maintain current rates, with market focus on forward guidance and economic projections. These decisions, influenced by recent inflation data and geopolitical developments, are poised to significantly impact global liquidity and risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Global Central Banks in Focus: Fed, BoJ, BoE Meetings This Week

details: The U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI) for May rose more than expected, with a 1.1% monthly increase, pushing the annual PPI to 6.5%. Core PPI, excluding volatile food and energy costs, also exceeded forecasts. This stronger-than-anticipated inflation data complicates the Federal Reserve's policy outlook by potentially suggesting a need for a longer period of restrictive monetary policy, which led to Bitcoin retracing some of its earlier gains.
title: US Producer Inflation Jumps Past Forecasts, Weighs on Fed Outlook
